name: Alior Bank SA
reason: Polish retail/SME bank whose EPS went PLN 2.26 (2019) and -2.39 (2020) to 18.19 (2025) on the rate cycle (0.96x of 10y peak), 10y avg ROE only 11.9% and consensus FY1 -26%, with state-linked control via PZU; not a through-cycle best-in-class bank.

name: Lloyds Banking Group plc
reason: UK mortgage-heavy bank with EPS flat-to-down at GBP 0.08 (2015) vs 0.07 (2025), 10y avg ROE 8.4% and NIM-driven outlook plus motor-finance redress exposure; no growth record in the zero-rate years.

name: Prosus N.V.
reason: Holding company whose adjusted EPS (USD 1.08 in 2019 to 3.73 in 2025) is driven by its Tencent stake and loss-making-to-breakeven EM internet assets (EBIT margin -43% to +3.1%), with adjusted-vs-GAAP gap ~-50% and acquisitions 8x FCF; value depends on stake valuation and capital allocation rather than forecastable operating earnings.

name: Deutsche EuroShop SE
reason: German shopping-centre owner with FFO flat at EUR 1.83 (2014) to 1.95 (2025), net debt/EBITDA 8.0x, consensus FY2-3 FFO declining and a now-controlling bidder; structurally challenged retail property with no growth route.

name: Alpha Bank S.A.
reason: Greek bank recovering from crisis (10y avg ROE -0.3%, share count +19.6%/yr from recapitalisations) with EPS at a 10y high of EUR 0.36 on the rate cycle and NPL clean-up; credit/rate driven, no through-cycle record.

name: Alstom SA
reason: Rolling-stock maker with EBIT margin of 3.6% (10y avg 4.6%), adjusted EPS EUR 1.35 below the EUR 2.13 2018 peak after the Bombardier deal, negative 10y FCF conversion (-0.56) and 63% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap; contract-execution economics are poor.

name: Piraeus Bank S.A.
reason: Greek bank with repeated losses and massive dilution (shares +68.5%/yr over 10y, avg ROE -0.6%) now earning EUR 0.82 EPS on the rate cycle; no through-cycle record and balance-sheet history fails the recession test.

name: UniCredit S.p.A.
reason: EPS rose from EUR 1.48 (2019) to a 10y high of 6.89 (2025) on higher rates plus buybacks after a 2016 loss of EUR -8.9, 10y avg ROE 4.9% and acquisitive M&A strategy; peak-NIM earnings not forecastable through cycle.

name: DEUTZ AG
reason: Cyclical diesel-engine maker with EBIT margin 4.2% (10y avg 2.8%), adjusted EPS EUR 0.37 vs 0.80 peak, 10y avg ROIC 6.7% and acquisitions 2.6x FCF; energy-transition threat to its core diesel product.

name: EUROBANK S.A.
reason: Greek bank whose EPS of EUR 0.37 (0.95x of 10y peak) rests on post-crisis NPL clean-up and the rate cycle, with 28%/yr share dilution historically and 10y avg ROE 9.6%; credit/rate-driven, not best-in-class through cycle.

name: Dampskibsselskabet NORDEN A/S
reason: Dry-bulk/product-tanker operator whose EPS swung from -5.81 (2015) to 90.04 (2022) and back to 4.10 (2025) in reporting currency; earnings set by freight rates.

name: EVN AG
reason: Austrian utility majority-owned by the State of Lower Austria with EPS EUR 2.45 (2025) below the 2.97 2023 energy-crisis peak, negative FCF yield and consensus FY2-3 EPS growth of -3.7%/+4.7%; regulated/commodity earnings with growth below 7%.

name: 3i Infrastructure PLC
reason: Listed infrastructure investment trust whose 'earnings' are portfolio valuation gains (EPS GBP 0.20 in 2015 to 0.36 in 2024, 1.9% 10y CAGR) and whose own target is an 8-10% total return; NAV/discount-rate driven, not an operating business.

name: Azimut Holding Spa
reason: Italian asset/wealth manager with EPS EUR 1.02 (2016) to 3.71 (2025) but earnings swing with performance fees and markets (2018 -39%, consensus FY1 -8.6%) at a 82nd-pctile EBIT margin; capital-markets-driven earnings, not forecastable under the US wealth-manager standard.

name: Noba Bank Group AB
reason: Recently listed Nordic consumer-credit lender (Bank Norwegian/Nordax) with only two years of EPS (SEK 4.00 to 6.82) under private-equity control; unsecured consumer lending is credit-cycle driven with no through-cycle record.

name: Solaria Energia y Medio Ambiente S.A.
reason: Spanish solar IPP with EBIT margin at 110% (100th pctile) from asset-rotation gains, net debt/EBITDA 5.4x and FCF yield -26.7%; earnings set by power prices and asset sales and growth is leverage-funded.

name: BNP Paribas Bank Polska Spolka Akcyjna
reason: Polish subsidiary bank whose EPS jumped from PLN 1.19 (2021) to a 10y high of 20.58 (2025) on Polish rates, 10y avg ROE 7.2% and consensus FY1 -28.7%; rate-cycle peak earnings with CHF-mortgage legal overhang.

name: Intesa Sanpaolo S.p.A.
reason: Italy's best-run large bank, but EPS doubled from EUR 0.24 (2019) to a 10y high of 0.53 (2025) mainly on the rate cycle, 10y avg ROE 9.8% and consensus FY3 growth slows to 7.7%; good but not a through-cycle compounder independent of NIM.

name: Sixt SE
reason: Car-rental company with EPS EUR 6.09 (0.67x of the 2018 peak), net debt/EBITDA 5.0x, 10y FCF conversion 0.15 and a 2020 loss; fleet residual values and travel cycles make earnings cyclical and capital intensive.

name: Bank of Cyprus Holdings Plc
reason: Cypriot bank with losses in 2017-20, EPS of EUR 1.10 near the 10y high on rates, revenue CAGR -4%/yr and consensus FY2-3 growth of only 2.9%/4.2%; rate-driven, no growth route.
